AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How can compost be used in a garden? (1 mark)
   A. Feed it to fish
   B. Mix it in planting holes or spread it around crops
   C. Throw it away
   D. Use it to build a wall

2. How wet should a compost heap be? (1 mark)
   A. Covered by a pool of water
   B. Completely dry
   C. Damp like a squeezed sponge
   D. Dripping wet

3. What is the danger of burning charcoal in a closed room? (1 mark)
   A. It creates rain
   B. It makes the room too cold
   C. It makes the walls bigger
   D. It gives off a poisonous gas

4. Where should kerosene be stored? (1 mark)
   A. Near the fire
   B. In a labelled container with a tight cap, away from children and fire
   C. In an open bowl
   D. In a water bottle on the table

5. Which of these is a small wild animal that can destroy crops? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Cow
   C. Weaver bird
   D. Goat

6. Which of these is a peaceful way of protecting fruit from birds? (1 mark)
   A. Covering trees with a light net
   B. Burning the trees
   C. Setting traps that kill
   D. Poisoning the birds

7. Why should a seedbed for tiny seeds be fine? (1 mark)
   A. Lumps help seeds
   B. It is a school rule
   C. Tiny seeds cannot push through big lumps
   D. Fine soil makes seeds bigger

8. How can a person without a garden grow tiny-seeded crops? (1 mark)
   A. On a road
   B. On hard rock
   C. Only in a forest
   D. In a container seedbed with drainage holes

9. Which of these crops has tiny seeds sown directly? (1 mark)
   A. Pawpaw tree
   B. Avocado
   C. Coconut
   D. Millet

10. How fine should the soil in the seedbed be? (1 mark)
   A. Crumbly like brown sugar
   B. Full of big clods
   C. Wet like mud
   D. Hard like stone

11. Why should a container seedbed have holes at the bottom? (1 mark)
   A. To make it lighter
   B. Insects can leave
   C. Extra water can drain out
   D. Seeds can escape

12. What is a tree tomato? (1 mark)
   A. A climbing vine
   B. A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands
   C. A vegetable that grows underground
   D. A cereal

13. What do flowers become in a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. Fruits
   B. Roots
   C. Trunks
   D. Soil

14. What do roots of a fruit tree do? (1 mark)
   A. Collect sunlight
   B. Make fruits
   C. Produce seeds
   D. Hold the tree and take in water and food

15. At what depth should the seedling be planted? (1 mark)
   A. Very deep
   B. Upside down
   C. The same depth as it was in the bag
   D. On top of the ground

16. Which practice keeps children safe when harvesting fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Pull the branch down hard
   B. Climb all trees
   C. Use a picking pole and take turns
   D. Push each other

17. What is the young one of a hen called? (1 mark)
   A. Kid
   B. Lamb
   C. Chick
   D. Calf

18. What is the meat of sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Bacon
   B. Mutton
   C. Pork
   D. Beef

19. What is meant by income from animals? (1 mark)
   A. Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
   B. Manure used
   C. Food eaten at home
   D. Feathers

20. What is a male sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Ram
   B. Cock
   C. Billy
   D. Bull

21. Which of these is an animal welfare need? (1 mark)
   A. Being hit
   B. Clean water always available
   C. Living in mud
   D. No shelter

22. What does variety mean in eating? (1 mark)
   A. Eating slowly
   B. Eating many different kinds of food
   C. Eating a lot
   D. Eating one food only

23. Which food is a good source of protein and cheap in many homes? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Sugar
   C. Beans
   D. Soda

24. About how long are eggs boiled for hard-boiled eggs? (1 mark)
   A. One second
   B. About 10 minutes
   C. About 10 seconds
   D. About 5 hours

25. What is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Storing food
   B. Preparing food using heat
   C. Washing food
   D. Cutting food

26. Which food is usually boiled? (1 mark)
   A. Potatoes
   B. Mandazi
   C. Chips
   D. Bhajia

27. What is the first thing to do with leftover cooked food? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it in the road
   B. Leave it on the floor
   C. Cover it and store it safely
   D. Leave it in the sun

28. Which is a disadvantage of too much frying? (1 mark)
   A. Too much oil is not good for health
   B. It uses no heat
   C. It removes all flavour
   D. It makes food cold

29. Why do farmers and cleaners wear personal protective equipment? (1 mark)
   A. To keep food hot
   B. To make work slower
   C. To look tall
   D. To protect the body from dirt, injury and germs

30. What is personal hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping our own bodies clean to stay healthy
   B. Cleaning the compound
   C. Washing cars
   D. Cooking food

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. List four safety rules when cooking. (4 marks)

32. Name three PPE items and what each protects. (3 marks)

33. Prepare a balanced menu for one day for a Grade 4 child using local foods and explain why it is balanced. (5 marks)

34. Explain the difference between green and brown materials for compost, with an example of each. (3 marks)

35. Name three products we get from cattle. (3 marks)

36. Give three uses of chickens. (3 marks)

37. Write a plan for growing a passion fruit plant from planting to harvest. (5 marks)

38. Give three uses of goats. (3 marks)

39. Explain the difference between variety and proportion in a meal. (3 marks)

40. Give three benefits of using compost manure on the farm. (3 marks)

41. Name two woody fruit trees and two climbing fruit crops. (4 marks)

42. Give three uses of sheep. (3 marks)

43. Explain why it is best to choose fruits that suit your locality. (3 marks)

44. Design a hygiene log for one week. List five practices to record and explain how you will use it. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Mix it in planting holes or spread it around crops
   Compost feeds crops and improves the soil.

2. C — Damp like a squeezed sponge
   Too dry stops rotting and too wet makes the heap smell sour.

3. D — It gives off a poisonous gas
   Charcoal fumes can make people ill or worse.

4. B — In a labelled container with a tight cap, away from children and fire
   Kerosene catches fire easily and is poisonous.

5. C — Weaver bird
   Weaver birds and other birds eat grain crops.

6. A — Covering trees with a light net
   A net keeps birds away without harming them.

7. C — Tiny seeds cannot push through big lumps
   Tiny seeds have little food and are weak.

8. D — In a container seedbed with drainage holes
   A box or tin with holes and fine soil works well.

9. D — Millet
   Millet has tiny seeds that are sown where the crop stays.

10. A — Crumbly like brown sugar
   Fine crumbly soil lets seeds come up easily.

11. C — Extra water can drain out
   Waterlogged soil rots seeds and roots.

12. B — A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands
   Tree tomato is a woody tree fruit.

13. A — Fruits
   Fruits develop from flowers.

14. D — Hold the tree and take in water and food
   Roots anchor and absorb.

15. C — The same depth as it was in the bag
   Planting too deep can rot the stem.

16. C — Use a picking pole and take turns
   Use safe methods.

17. C — Chick
   A chick is a young chicken.

18. B — Mutton
   Mutton is sheep meat.

19. A — Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
   Farmers sell products to earn money.

20. A — Ram
   A ram is a male sheep.

21. B — Clean water always available
   Animals need water, feed, shelter, health care and kind treatment.

22. B — Eating many different kinds of food
   Variety means different foods.

23. C — Beans
   Beans are protein-rich.

24. B — About 10 minutes
   Ten minutes of gentle boiling makes hard eggs.

25. B — Preparing food using heat
   Cooking uses heat to make food safe and tasty.

26. A — Potatoes
   Potatoes are commonly boiled.

27. C — Cover it and store it safely
   Covered food stays safe from flies.

28. A — Too much oil is not good for health
   Too much oil can harm health.

29. D — To protect the body from dirt, injury and germs
   PPE is clothing and gear that protects us from harm.

30. A — Keeping our own bodies clean to stay healthy
   Personal hygiene is care of the body.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cook with an adult; turn handles inward; use a dry cloth for hot pots; open lids away from the face; keep water away from hot oil (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Breakfast: porridge and egg; lunch: ugali, beans and sukuma wiki; supper: rice, fish and cabbage with fruit. It includes energy, body-building and protective foods in every day.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for a menu with all groups, 2 marks for correct explanation.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Green materials are fresh and wet such as fresh grass or peelings. Brown materials are dry such as dry leaves or straw.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for correct examples.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Milk, beef, hides and skins, manure, or draught power (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each product.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eggs, meat, manure, feathers and income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: Build a trellis; dig and prepare a hole with compost; plant a seedling; water and mulch; tie the stem to the support; weed and prune; harvest ripe fruits and wash before eating.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Meat, milk, skins, manure and income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Variety is eating many kinds of food; proportion is eating the right amount of each kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for variety, 1 mark for proportion, 1 mark for an example.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: It feeds crops, it softens the soil and helps it to hold water, and it is cheap because it uses waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct benefit.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Woody: guava, tree tomato, mango; climbing: passion fruit, grapes, kiwi, blackberry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mutton, wool (some breeds), skins, manure, income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: They grow better in the local climate, give more fruit, and need less care and cost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Practices: washed hands before meals, brushed teeth twice, bathed, clean clothes, drank safe water. Tick each day, count ticks at the end, and improve the practice with fewest ticks.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for practices and table, 2 marks for use.
